audit.summary: The spectral NCL identifiability theorem is transferred without justification to CSR's different loss. Literal and normalized readings were checked, including an explicit reconstruction-compatible ambiguity.
limitations: Limitations: No author-code execution or empirical timing/accuracy reproduction.
Limitations: Not a refutation of the cited theorem under its own spectral assumptions.
Limitations: Full text/multimodal pipelines not audited.
Limitations: No later-version or global erratum search.
Limitations: The normalized ambiguity is for the paper's reconstruction equations plus normalized contrastive loss; no full released-pipeline global-minimum claim.

P1 — Counterevidence: Released code normalizes features and uses two duplicate views, defeating the unnormalized scale-escape criticism alone. The normalized ambiguity concerns that contrastive reading combined with paper Eq5. Optional input preprocessing and residual-variance-normalized auxiliary loss in the release prevent treating the zero-residual example as a full executable-pipeline optimizer. The original spectral theorem is not refuted.
The original report's complete scope, counterevidence and unresolved questions are retained below.
This import checks publication format and identity; it does not repeat scientific review.
Independent human scientific review is pending; author adoption has not been requested.

proposition.claim: CSR Eq6 can invoke Wang et al. Theorem5 and theoretically guarantee identifiability/disentanglement and increased latent utilization.
